placeholders.@FABLE_ID@: A Fable-class id injected at test time. A real Fable id never lands in a fixture.

notes: Contract section 5.4 (R3-f). Each vector is a reply whose receipt is the complete receipt. The tests take the receipt file to be the compact JSON of reply.receipt after the Fable id is injected, so receipt_sha256 is the sha256 of those UTF-8 bytes. A real receiver hashes its own file. The limit is 16384 UTF-8 bytes of the reply as sent; the reference serializes compact JSON with separators , and : and no ASCII escaping. A trimmed reply removes observed_models entries from the end, one at a time, until it fits, never the root entry and never an entry whose model matches fableId. It keeps the order and every other receipt field, and observed_models is never added to unobserved. expect.kept_always lists units that must survive. A reply still over the limit becomes kind failed, reason reply-too-large, receipt null. halt_acks rows are round 4 (R4-b): a halt ack has receipt null and nothing to trim. The receiver splits the stopped job ids, in stop order, across whole halted acks of at most limit_bytes each, with the same job_id, reason halt and halt_msg_id. Every id is in exactly one ack, no ack is empty, and a halt that stopped no job gets one ack with an empty list. Split points depend on the sender's serialization, so a reader takes the union and never relies on them.
